title: Astronomers study an off-center tidal disruption event and use it to bound how common offset black holes are
summary: A paper on TDE 2025abcr argues the flare—found by ZTF and followed up with SOAR and Swift—was a tidal disruption event about 9.3 kiloparsecs from its host’s nucleus, offering a first concrete example of off-nuclear supermassive black holes while suggesting highly offset TDEs are under 10% of the nuclear rate, though the black hole’s origin and survey completeness remain unresolved.

claims.text: The paper explicitly states that TDE 2025abcr was identified by a custom off-nuclear implementation of the machine-learning classifier tdescore, and that follow-up observations confirmed it as a TDE-H+He.

sources.title: TDE 2025abcr: A Tidal Disruption Event in the Outskirts of a Massive Galaxy

claims.text: The paper says the classification was driven by a high lower bound on blackbody temperature, a poor Type Ia supernova fit (sncosmo chi-square per degree of freedom = 4.5), and a best-fit temperature that increased with time rather than cooling (+87 K/day).

sources.title: TDE 2025abcr: A Tidal Disruption Event in the Outskirts of a Massive Galaxy

claims.text: The paper describes luminous UV and soft X-ray emission plus spectroscopic signatures that distinguish TDEs from supernovae and other contaminants.

sources.title: TDE 2025abcr: A Tidal Disruption Event in the Outskirts of a Massive Galaxy

claims.text: The spectral sequence shows a blue continuum with little apparent cooling, broad H lines, and a blended He II lambda 4686 plus N III lambda 4640 feature, resembling known TDEs.

sources.title: TDE 2025abcr: A Tidal Disruption Event in the Outskirts of a Massive Galaxy

claims.text: The transient was measured to lie 9.5 arcseconds, or 9.3 kpc projected distance, from the host-galaxy nucleus.

sources.title: TDE 2025abcr: A Tidal Disruption Event in the Outskirts of a Massive Galaxy

claims.text: The paper's localization relies on archival LS DR10 imaging that marks the transient and host center, and Figure 2 says no source is seen at the transient position to m = 23.78 / M = -12.78, ruling out a bright dwarf-galaxy origin at that position.

sources.title: TDE 2025abcr: A Tidal Disruption Event in the Outskirts of a Massive Galaxy

claims.text: The source was not identified by any other ongoing TDE search effort because of its offset location, and it was the first off-nuclear tdescore discovery not also found by the classic or unbiased selections.

claims.text: The paper states that the rate of highly offset TDEs (greater than or equal to about 3 kpc) can be constrained to less than 10% of the nuclear TDE rate.

claims.text: The paper explicitly names three alternative transient classes considered for TDE 2025abcr beyond the TDE interpretation: an exotic supernova, an LFBOT, and an AGN flare.

sources.title: TDE 2025abcr: A Tidal Disruption Event in the Outskirts of a Massive Galaxy

claims.text: The paper excludes an interacting supernova origin because the observed X-ray emission is soft rather than the hard X-rays typical of interacting supernovae, and the overall UV/X-ray/spectroscopic behavior matches a TDE instead.

sources.title: TDE 2025abcr: A Tidal Disruption Event in the Outskirts of a Massive Galaxy

claims.text: The paper excludes an AGN-flare interpretation because the host nucleus lacks classic AGN signatures, specifically Balmer lines and [O III] λ4959/λ5007 emission.

sources.title: TDE 2025abcr: A Tidal Disruption Event in the Outskirts of a Massive Galaxy

claims.text: The paper also excludes an AGN origin because the X-ray behavior is not the rapid hour-scale variability expected for many AGN flares.

sources.title: TDE 2025abcr: A Tidal Disruption Event in the Outskirts of a Massive Galaxy

claims.text: The paper treats LFBOT as a credible competing class but argues the event does not fit that picture, instead resembling known TDEs in its multiwavelength and spectroscopic properties.

sources.title: TDE 2025abcr: A Tidal Disruption Event in the Outskirts of a Massive Galaxy

claims.text: The paper’s strongest discriminants against non-TDE alternatives are the high lower bound on blackbody temperature, the poor Type Ia supernova fit, a temperature that rises rather than cools, luminous UV and soft X-ray emission, and TDE-like spectral features including broad H lines plus He II/N III.
